short: Explicit tone stage (M06) is new in Mandarin lip reading but standard: no repeated runs, and its 1.59-point CER margin bundles tone with video attention; tone without video is worse (42.23%).
position: CSSMCM [@zhao2019cascade] adds an explicit tone stage between pinyin syllables and characters (M06) and builds CMLR with ASR-generated references (M11). Separate tone recognition existed in Mandarin speech recognition [@hirose2006tone], but no prior Mandarin lip-reading study had a tone stage [@zhang2019lipchnet; @zhou2019modality; @yang2019lrw1000]. Its support is a 1.59-point CER margin over a re-implemented LipCH-Net that shares CSSMCM's first stage, so the margin bundles tone with video attention, and the tone-without-video variant is worse (42.23% against 34.07%); no repeated runs are reported, so it is standard rather than ahead. CMLR's labels are iFLYTEK output with no reported check, which the authors concede is noisy, while LipCH-Net and LRW-1000 checked their transcripts by hand. All 11 hosts appear in training and test; on LipFormer's split with 2 unseen hosts CSSMCM reaches 50.08% CER [@xue2023lipformer]. The same group's [concurrent] LIBS reaches 31.27% without tones using an audio-trained teacher [@zhao2020hearing].
